mishnah_berurah.he:
(א) בפחות מעשרה - דהוא דבר שבקדושה ואינו בפחות מי' דכתיב ונקדשתי בתוך בני ישראל ואתיא בגז"ש דתוך תוך כתיב הכא תוך בני ישראל וכתיב התם הבדלו מתוך העדה הזאת ואין עדה פחותה מעשרה:
(ב) גדולים - לאפוקי קטנים שהם פחותים מי"ג ויום אחד אע"ג דקטן משלים למנין שבעה כדלקמן בסימן רפ"ב ס"ג מ"מ אינו משלים לעשרה:
(ג) בני חורין - לאפוקי עבדים:
(ד) התחילו בעשרה וכו' - ואם התחיל רק ברכו לבד לא הוי התחלה בזה [פמ"ג]:
(ה) ויצאו מקצתן - ובנשתיירו רובן דהיינו ששה סגי ולא בעינן רובא דמנכר ועל היוצאין נאמר ועוזבי ה' יכלו ואף בין גברא לגברא אסור וכי מותר לצאת בין גברא לגברא היינו דוקא בנשארו עשרה [אחרונים]:
(ו) גומרין - היינו בחול כל השלשה וביו"ט חמשה ובשבת כל השבעה קרואים אבל לא יוסיפו על זה ואומרים קדיש שאחר הקריאה אבל למפטיר לא יקרא דהוא ענין אחר ולא נגרר בתר קריאת התורה וכ"ש שלא יפטיר אח"כ בנביא ויש שכתבו שמ"מ טוב לומר הפטרה בנביא בלא ברכותיה. ובהפטרה נמי דינא הכי דאם התחילו ברכות של הפטרה בעשרה ויצאו מקצתן גומרין לומר ההפטרה עם ברכותיה שאחר כך:
mishnah_berurah.en:
(1) With less than ten — for it is a matter of sanctity, and it is not [done] with less than ten, as it is written: "and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel"; and it is derived by gezeirah shavah: "among," "among" is written here "among the children of Israel," and it is written there: "Separate yourselves from among this congregation"; and a congregation is not less than ten.

(2) Adults — to exclude minors, who are less than thirteen years and one day; for although a minor completes the count of seven, as below siman 282, s.k. 3 — nevertheless he does not complete [the count] to ten.

(3) Free men — to exclude slaves.

(4) They began with ten, etc. — and if he began only with the blessing alone, this is not considered a beginning for this [matter] [Peri Megadim].

(5) And some of them left — and when the majority remained, meaning six suffice; and we do not require a recognizable majority; and of those who leave it is said: "and those who forsake the the Master shall perish." And it is forbidden even between one man and another [aliyah]. And when it is permitted to leave between one man and another, this is specifically when ten remain [acharonim].

(6) They finish — meaning on a weekday all three [readers], and on Yom Tov five, and on Shabbat all seven readers; but they do not add beyond this, and they say Kaddish after the reading. But for the maftir he does not read, for it is a separate matter and is not drawn after Torah reading; and all the more so he does not read haftara afterward from the Prophets. And there are those who wrote that nevertheless it is good to say the haftara from the Prophets without its blessings. And for the haftara too the law is thus: if they began the blessings of the haftara with ten and some left, they finish saying the haftara with its blessings afterward.

peri_megadim.en: And if [an error is found] — Ateret Zekenim. Here it implies that there are three views. (1) The view of Mahari Bei Rav, the teacher of Beit Yosef, that whenever an error is found — if he finished the reading and blessed after it, and afterward the error was found — b'dieved the reading in the invalid Torah scroll is valid, and they complete until the count of seven on Shabbat, or six on Yom Tov and Yom Kippur, and four and three on Rosh Chodesh and weekdays, in a valid scroll (and so in Beit Yosef Yoreh Deah 279, and Levush there, and so he wrote here "and they complete," and they need not read seven anew), for b'dieved we rely on Rambam in his responsum that reading in an invalid scroll is valid; and that missing one letter did not fulfill the mitzvah of writing a Torah scroll — see Beit Yosef Yoreh Deah 279; and Ran added that Torah reading is an enactment of the prophets and does not impede b'dieved, for the difference between a Torah scroll and tefillin and mezuzah is only regarding missing one letter not fulfilling the mitzvah of writing, but for reading it is an enactment of the prophets — see there; and so Levush Yoreh Deah 279, seif 2, see there. And therefore Parah Adumah and Zachor — some say they are d'oraisa — require study in this, that perhaps in an invalid Torah scroll it does not help even b'dieved if they read the entire parasha and afterward found an error on this column and the like — siman 146, s.k. 2, Parah and Zachor, which require ten d'oraisa, and Magen Avraham siman 488, and as we need to say below. And all this if he already blessed the closing blessing on the invalid scroll; but if in the middle of his reading they found an error, even if they read much — one does not bless the closing blessing on the invalid scroll, for this is l'chatchila; rather they take out another and read there (it implies three verses in a valid scroll) and bless the closing blessing there; and all the more if before three verses — they read in the second and bless the closing blessing, and not the first. And Mordekhai holds: if they read three verses, he blesses the closing blessing there b'dieved; and even if they did not read three verses, he says the error from memory where it is impossible, and completes three verses and blesses, and afterward they take out a valid one. And Rama in the gloss explained between the views: whoever did not read three verses reads in a valid scroll (and if possible three verses; and if the sedra is finished, he finishes thus) and blesses after it and not before it — and this is Mahari Bei Rav; and when he read three verses, he ruled like Mordekhai that he blesses the closing blessing on the invalid scroll; and if he cannot stop, being two verses before the parasha, then he reads the error from memory like Mordekhai. And therefore it should have been written "some say"; and in Levush he wrote here "some say" — if he read three verses he blesses on the invalid scroll; and in Yoreh Deah 279 he did not write "some say," which implies his view is like view (1) plainly: that in the middle of his parasha, even if he read much, he finishes in a valid scroll and blesses the closing blessing there — unlike his teacher here. But one who examines Beit Yosef here and Yoreh Deah may say that Mahari Bei Rav too, in the middle of reading when he did not read three verses — if he read three verses, he admits one blesses the closing blessing on the invalid scroll, as appears from the flow of Shach's words in Yoreh Deah 279, s.k. 3; and so too from Taz there in what he answered from Kiddushin on Yom Kippur: therefore one does not bless the opening blessing here on the second, for he has not yet fulfilled any mitzvah since he did not read three verses — if he read three verses, all agree he blesses the closing blessing on the first Torah scroll; and this teaches as I wrote, and there are only two views. And Rama in the author ruled completely like Mahari Bei Rav. And from what is written in Yoreh Deah "he raised," etc. — you will see that Rama in the gloss here may be that he ruled completely like Mahari Bei Rav, and one does not read an error from memory in any case, unlike Mordekhai; and if so, when he read three verses and cannot stop, there being two verses to the parasha, they take out another and finish there — for otherwise it is difficult from Kiddushin on Yom Kippur: whenever he read three verses the mitzvah is done and it is fitting to bless the opening blessing on the second, as Yoreh Deah writes; and therefore in such a case he reads from memory; and also the last [aliyah] likewise reads from memory on account of burdening the congregation — see there; and for the maftir they take out another, since they say Kaddish there is no burden — see there; and for the maftir likewise he reads the error from memory, like the last — such is his view there. And for practical law, Magen Avraham, letter 4, will explain below. And on the last [aliyah], Taz [holds that] even if only one verse, he completes in the invalid scroll.

mechaber.en: If each Chumash [i.e. each of the five books of the Torah] was written separately, even if they were each rolled like a Torah scroll, we do not read from it until all five [books] are sewn together. {Rama: Gloss: And they must be rolled like a Torah scroll. But our Chumashim, even if all five books are [bound] together, we do not make the blessing over it (Mordekhai - end of chapter "Hanizkin" and end of chapter "Hakometz", Teshuvot Ramba"n - siman 187 and 199, Rabbeinu Yerucham - Netiv 2, third volume, Agur - in the name of Shibolei Leket, Mahari"k - shoresh 68, and Kol Bo, Positive Mitzvot, chapter 9 of Laws of a Torah Scroll). And in a place that has a Torah scroll, but there is no prayer leader [who is reading for others] who is an expert in reading using the correct cantillation marks by heart, I saw that some have a custom that the prayer leader reads from the Chumash using the markings [i.e. the vowels and/or cantillation marks], and the one who is called up reads after [the prayer leader] from the valid Torah scroll.}

חסירות עט״ז נחים נסתרים שאין קריאתם משתנה בשביל זה אין מוציאין אחרת ובחיסר אות נא נראה מוציאין אחרת (להשוות דיעות הפוסקים ובזה מתורץ מ״ש האגור בשם הרא״ש דאין מוציאין אחרת שזה היפך מ״ש הרא״ש עב״י אלא בחסר ויתר מיירי עיין פרישה) והביא שו״ת מהר״ם לובלין סי׳ פ״ד (עמ״א אות ח׳) דבאין ס״ת אחרת והתחילו כבר לקרות ומצאו טעות ישלימו מנין הקרואים בס״ת זו ומברכין לפניה ואחריה ומשמע שם אפי׳ לכתחלה מוציאין וקורין ואנו נוהגין כרמ״א בזה כל שלא התחילו אין מוציאין אף בשחרית כיש פוסלין אם לא שחומש א׳ שלם ואם התחילו יגמרו מנין הקרואים אם אין ס״ת אחרת ובמנחה דאין אלא משום יושבי קרנות מ״מ אפשר דגומרין כל שהתחילו דמ״מ תקנה היא כמו ב׳ וה׳ ומה לי מנחה או ב׳ וה׳ ועמ״א אוח ח׳. ואף שמט״ז משמע שאותו הסדק אין נראה לעין משמע דחסר תיבה אין מורין כן הרי בשו״ת מור״ם ז״ל הורה כן וכ״כ המ״א ח׳ רק לכתחלה אין מוציאין:
ודע כל שיש מחלוקת הפוסקים אי הוי זה טעות או לאו אין להוציא אחרת דהוי ס״ס שמא הלכת כר״מ בתשובה דקורין בפסולה דע״ז אנו סומכין דיעבד ושמא הלכה כמ״ד בפסול כזה אין פסול ואף דכתבנו במקום אחר בספק ברכה חומר לא תשא י״ל דס״ס לא מהני מ״מ המעיין בסימן תפ״ט בספק אם סיפר יברך בבאר הימים ע״ש ס״ח דהוי ס״ס א״כ משמע דמהני ס״ס לברך ואי״ה בש״ה יבואר זה:
אם נדבק אות באות אפי׳ בשבת א״צ להוציא אחרת די״ל על הרשב״א בזה ט״ז ב״ח סי׳ ל״ב אות י״ח ועמ״א ז׳ ומסתימת הב״ח בל״ב וט״ז משמע אף נדבקה באמצע י״ל דאין מוציאין אחרת. ובנטף שעוה ומכוסה עב וא״א לקרות התיבה כלל עסי׳ ש״מ בט״ז וא״ר א׳ וה׳ והנה י״ל כל הראוי לבילה כמו לגיור סומכין על הרשב״א ומיהו משום דאסור לקרות בע״פ י״ל וקרא בחומש ואל יוציאו אחרת אבל כשנטף שעוה על מקום אח׳ י״ל דסומכין ודאי כמ״ש ועי׳ שו״ת מעיל צדקה סי׳ כ״ה עמ״ש בקמ״א במ״א ט׳ ככתבין ולא קריין ל״ש על פה יע״ש:
כתב בשו״ת מעיל צדקה להגאון מוהר״ר יונה ל״ס ז״ל סימן כ״ט בפ׳ נח ויהי כל ימי נח (ראשית ט׳ כ״ט) כצ״ל וי״א ויהיו אבל עיקר ויהי בלא וי״ו ומ״מ בשבת אין להוציא אחרת יע״ש. הנה כל שיש ספק אין מוציאין ואמנם למדתי מדבריו ז״ל כי אמרינן חסר ומלא אין מוציאין בנח נסתר באמצע התיבה שאין משתנה הקריאה כלל משא״כ כתב ויהיו במקום ויהי פסול הוא אע״ג דוי״ו נח נסתר הרי נשתנה הקריאה מחמת הכתיבה עמ״א ז׳ רחבה רחבו ושם יבואר אי״ה. ע״ש אש דת חד מלה וקריין תרין ואם בב׳ שיטין אפשר פסול כמו כתיבין ולא קריין דשינוי פוסל בהם עכ״ל:
וז״ל הר״מ ז״ל פרק עשירי מס״ת ה״א עשרים דברים פוסלים הס״ת. והנה עשה פתוחה סתומה או להיפוך פסולה ומוציאין אחרת אבל אם לא הניח ט׳ אותיות חלק עש״ך י״ד סי׳ ער״ה די״א ג׳ אותיות סגי דיעבד וא״כ כשיש ג׳ אותיות אין מוציאין אחרת בספק פלוגתא כמש״ל דהוי ס״ס. וכן יצא השם חוץ לדף או תלה מקצת השם די״א דכשר הוא עמ״א סי׳ ל״ב אות מ״ז כל ספק אין מוציאין אחרת ועי״ד רע״ו בש״ך אות ז׳ וט״ז ד׳ ובר״מ פ״א מתפילין הי״ו תלה מקצת השם פסול ובפרק עשירי מס״ת ה״א לא מנה בכלל הכ׳ דברים זה ואפשר לאין קורין ברבים דוקא הנך עשרים הא מקצת השם אפשר ספק הוא וקויין בו עכ״פ דהוי ס״ס ולפ״ז כל ספק פלוגתא אם פסולה או לאו יכולין לכתחלה לקרות בו מה״ט גופא דהוי ספק ספיקא:
אם נכנס ראש הלמ״ד באחת מאותיות (או אותיות הפשיטות נו״ן צד״י פ״א בתוך אותיות שתחתיה לטי״ת ושי״ן ועיין וכדומה) עיין סימן ל״ב סכ״ח ובט״ז ל״ב ובמ״א מ׳ שיש מכשירין א״כ פשיטא שאין מוציאין אתרת ואפשר אפילו קורא לכתחלה בברכה אם אין אחרת דשמא הלכה כר״מ בתשובה דקורין בס״ת פסולה אם אין אחרת וכמ״ש הר״ב בהג״ה יש מכשירין כה״ג ושמא כשירה הוא ועמ״א מזה אי״ה ואל תשיבני ממ״ש הב״ח בסימן ל״ב סעיף י״ג בסופו דבדיבוק אות לאות אין להוציא לכתחלה י״ל ביש כשירה או דקיי״ל דלא כרשב״א משא״כ בספק גמור. ואם מגיע אות בלי היקף גויל מתחלתו נמי אין מוציאין אחרת דסומכין על הרשב״א עמ״א ל״ב אות כ״ז יע״ש:
בי״ד סימן רע״ד סו״ז זיינ״ן שעטנ״ז ג״ץ יש ליזהר ובמנוקד או פיסוק טעמים פסול ולעיל בסי׳ ל״ו במ״א בשם הב״ח פוסל אם לא זיין שעטנ״ז ג״ץ והנה הר״מ מכשיר בזה בביאור פ״ז מס״ת ה״י וי״א ובמנוקד ופיסוק טעמים מכשיר מדלא מנה פרק עשירי כ״א כ׳ דברים עב״י י״ד שם וא״כ בפסולים אלו ל״מ דאין מוציאין אחרת אפילו לקרות לכתחלה באין ס״ת אחרת י״ל דקורין וצ״ע בזה:
והוי יודע דבי״ד רפ״א מנה הפסולים לכתוב וממזר יש פוסלין נמצא ביד עכו״ם ספק וסבור הייתי לומר גם בכה״ג הוי ספק פלוגתא והוי ס״ס שוב ראיתי דל״ד דס״ת שחיסר או טעות י״ל דמי לחומשין דאי לאו כבוד הציבור היו קורין בהם ובטעות ליכא כבוד הציבור כמו שיראה הרואה בפר״ח כאן הביא תשובת הרמב״ם ובכ״מ פ״י מס״ת יע״ש וא״כ דוקא כה״ג הא כל שכולה נכתבת בפיסול אין שם ס״ת עליה כלל ואפילו אותם שקראו דיעבד לא עלתה קריאה וצריך לקרות מראש הס״ת כשירה אם יש להם (כדעת הרא״ש בי״ד רע״ט וכ״ע מודים לזה ואף שהר״מ ז״ל פ״י מס״ת ה״א כ׳ ך׳ דברים ויש שם מעובד שלא לשמו ואפיקורס וכדומה שכולה בפיסול ומדכללו יחד שאין קורין בהם משמע חיסור נמי אף דיעבד וא״א בע״א אין קורין כלל צ״ל דלאו לכל מילי מדמי להדדי וכאמור:
כבר כתבנו אם אירע בפ׳ פרה או זכור טעות וקראו מקצת הפרשה דיש להוציא כשירה ולקרות מראש כדעת הרא״ש בי״ד רע״ט דהני י״א שהם ד״ת כבסימן קמ״ו ס״ב והמעיין בי״ד רע״ט כ״ע של היתר הוא דקריאה בציבור תקנת נביאים לא החמירו בה ואין בין ס״ת לתפילין לענין כתיבה מ״ע ד״ת א״כ בהני נמי ד״ת וחוזר מראש ובלא ברכה דאין מעכבת וגם ממרדכי הביאו הד״מ בי״ד רע״ט מוכח דאף באחרון ומפטיר אם יש להפסיק שם מוציאים אחרת כמ״ש במ״א אות וי״ו ועתה ראיתי בא״ר אות וי״ו הרגיש בזה יע״ש. וע׳ לבוש י״ד רע״ט וכאן ג״כ הטעם הואיל ותקנת נביאים הוא:
ויתר הדברים אי״ה יתבאר במ״א אות ז׳ ח״ט וכאן אין להאריך יותר:
עוד רגע אדבר כתב א״ר כאן אות ה׳ נמצא תיבה שלימה כפולה מוציאין אחרת דכל יתר כנטול דמי ולי צ״ע די״ל כה״ג י״ל כל הראוי לבילה כמו נדבקה אות באות ה״ה כאן ואף די״ל ומ״ש יתר כנטול זה בטריפות גמירי כך משא״כ כאן וצ״ע:
אמר ההדיוט הכותב כל מה ששמעתי מרבותי וקצת מה שהורוני משמים רשמתי ודאי ה׳ ס״ת ארוכים ורחבים מני ים ובעו״ה קלקול הזמנים. וכל אדם ירא לנפשו יזהר בזה בפרט סופרי סת״ם צא וראה מ״ש הצ״צ בסי׳ קי״ט לאחר שהורה היה ירא שמא לא כיון כהלכה והיה גדול בדורו ומה יענו כמונו היום לכן ירא כל איש לנפשו קודם שיורה דין וכדומה:
peri_megadim.en:
Missing [letters] — Ateret Zekenim: hidden nekudot whose reading does not change on account of this — one does not take out another; and for a missing letter it appears one takes out another (to harmonize the views of the poskim, and thereby is resolved what Agur wrote in the name of Rosh that one does not take out another — this is the opposite of what Rosh wrote explicitly, except that missing and extra letters are what is discussed — see Perishah). And he brought the responsum of Maharam Lublin siman 84 (Magen Avraham, letter 8): when there is no other Torah scroll and they already began to read and found an error, they complete the count of readers in this scroll and bless before and after it; and it is implied there that even l'chatchila they take out and read; and we practice like Rama in this: as long as they have not begun, they do not take out, even on Monday morning, if they invalidate it — unless one chumash is complete; and if they began, they complete the count of readers if there is no other Torah scroll. And for Minhah, which is only on account of the inhabitants of Keren HaRez — nevertheless it is possible they complete all that they began, for it is nevertheless an enactment like Monday and Thursday; and what difference to me whether Minhah or Monday and Thursday? And Magen Avraham, letter 8. And even though Taz implies that crack is not visible to the eye, it implies that a missing word — one does not rule thus; behold, in the responsum of Mordekhai he ruled thus, and so Magen Avraham, letter 8 — only l'chatchila one does not take out.

And know: whenever there is a dispute among the poskim whether this is an error or not, one does not take out another, for it is a double doubt: perhaps the halakha is like Rambam in his responsum that they read in an invalid scroll — on this we rely b'dieved; and perhaps the halakha is like those who hold that in such an invalid scroll it is not pasul. And even though we wrote in another place that in doubt of a blessing one is stringent — one may say that a double doubt does not help; nevertheless, one who examines siman 489, in doubt whether he counted, should bless — Beer Mayim Chayim, see there, s.k. 8, that it is a double doubt; if so, it is implied that a double doubt helps to bless; and therefore in siman 185 this will be explained.

If a letter stuck to a letter, even on Shabbat one need not take out another, for one may rely on Rashba in this — Taz, Bach siman 32, letter 18, and Magen Avraham, letter 7; and from the conclusion of Bach in siman 32 and Taz it is implied that even if it stuck in the middle, one may say one does not take out another. And regarding wax that dripped and covered thickly so one cannot read the word at all — siman 340, Taz, and one vav and one hei — one may say: whatever is fit for soaking, like for conversion, one relies on Rashba; however, because it is forbidden to read from memory, one may say he reads from a chumash and they do not take out another. But when wax dripped on one place, one may say they rely certainly as I wrote; and see responsum Ma'il Tzedakah siman 25; see what is written in Kamma, Magen Avraham, letter 9, as they write and do not read Parah from memory — see there.

He wrote in responsum Ma'il Tzedakah to the Gaon Maharar Yona, siman 29, on the parasha of Noach: "and it was all the days of Noach" (Genesis 9:29) — so it should be; and some [manuscripts have] "and they were," but the essence is "and it was" without a vav; and nevertheless on Shabbat one does not take out another — see there. Here, whenever there is a doubt, one does not take out another. But I learned from his words that we say: missing and full [letters] — one does not take out another; the vav of Noach is hidden in the middle of the word, so the reading does not change at all — unlike if it is written veyihu instead of vayehi, which is pasul, even though the vav of Noach is hidden, for the reading was changed on account of the writing — Magen Avraham, letter 7, rachava/rachavo, and there it will be explained below. "The fire of religion: one word and they read two" — and if in two lines it is possible [to read as] pasul, like ketiv and not kri, a change invalidates them — until here.

And these are his words — Rambam, chapter 10 of Laws of a Torah Scroll, halakhah 1: twenty things invalidate a Torah scroll. And here: he made open closed or the reverse — pasul, and they take out another. But if he did not leave nine letters in the section — as in ashekh, siman 14, siman 475 — some say three letters suffice b'dieved; if so, when there are three letters one does not take out another, in doubt of a dispute, as stated above, for it is a double doubt. And likewise if the Name went outside the column, or part of the Name was suspended — some say it is kosher d'oraita — Magen Avraham siman 32, letter 47: any doubt — one does not take out another; and see Rosh Akiva, letter 7, and Taz, letter 4, and Rambam chapter 1 of Laws of Tefillin: if a vav suspended part of the Name it is pasul; but in chapter 10 of Laws of a Torah Scroll, halakhah 1, he did not count this among the twenty — possibly because "they do not read publicly" applies only to those twenty; part of the Name is perhaps a doubt, and one may rely on it in any case, for it is a double doubt. And therefore any doubt of a dispute whether it is pasul or not — they may read from it l'chatchila, from the doubt itself, which is a double doubt.

If the head of a lamed entered one of the letters (or the nekudot of nun, tzadi, pei within letters under tet, shin, and the like) — see siman 32, s.k. 288, and Taz siman 32, and Magen Avraham, letter 40, that some validate it; if so, it is clear one does not take out ateret; and it is possible even to read l'chatchila with a blessing if there is no other, for perhaps the halakha is like Rambam in his responsum that they read in an invalid Torah scroll when there is no other — as Rama wrote in the gloss: some validate in such a case, and perhaps it is kosher — Magen Avraham from this will explain below. And do not answer me from what Bach wrote in siman 32, seif 13 at the end, that in adhesion of letter to letter one does not take out l'chatchila — one may say there is an opinion that it is kosher, or that we hold not like Rashba, unlike a complete doubt. And if a letter reaches without margin from the beginning of the parchment — likewise one does not take out another, for we rely on Rashba — Magen Avraham siman 32, letter 27, see there.

Yoreh Deah siman 274, s.k. 7: zein, she'atnez, gatz — one must be careful; and with vowels or tropes it is pasul. And above siman 36, Magen Avraham in the name of Bach, invalidates if it is not zein, she'atnez, gatz. And here Rambam validates this in the explanation of chapter 7 of Laws of a Torah Scroll, halakhah 10, and "some" validate with vowels and tropes, since in chapter 10 he did not count among the twenty-one items explicitly — if so, in these invalidations Rama holds one does not take out another, even to read l'chatchila when there is no other Torah scroll; one may say they read, and this requires study.

And know: in Yoreh Deah 481 he counted the invalidations for writing; mamzer — some invalidate [a scroll] found in the hand of a gentile — it is a doubt; and I thought to say that also in such a case it is a dispute-doubt and a double doubt. Again I saw: a Torah scroll that is missing or has an error — one may say it is like chumashim: if not for honor of the congregation they would read from them; and in error there is no honor of the congregation, as the viewer will see in Pri Chadash here, where he brought Rambam's responsum and many [cases] in chapter 10, see there. And if so, only in such a case; but whatever was entirely written in invalidity — there is no Torah scroll upon it at all; and even those who read — b'dieved their reading did not count, and they must read from the beginning of a valid Torah scroll if they have one (as the view of Rosh in Yoreh Deah 279, and all agree to this; and even though Rambam, chapter 10, halakhah 1, lists twenty-one things, and there is one worked not for its sake, and an apikores, and the like — all in invalidity; and since he included them together that one does not read from them, it implies missing letters too, even b'dieved; and it is impossible to say one reads from memory at all — it must be that they are not compared to each other in all matters, as stated).

We already wrote: if it occurred in the parasha of Parah or Zachor that there was an error and they read part of the parasha — one must take out a valid scroll and read from the beginning, as the view of Rosh in Yoreh Deah 279; for these are among those that are d'oraisa, as in siman 146, s.k. 2. And one who examines Yoreh Deah 279 — all the leniency is because reading in public is an enactment of the prophets, and they were not stringent about it; and there is no difference between a Torah scroll and tefillin regarding the mitzvah of writing d'oraisa; if so, in these too it is d'oraisa, and one returns from the beginning without a blessing, for it does not impede. And also from Mordekhai, Darkei Moshe brought in Beit Yosef Yoreh Deah 279, proves that even on the last [aliyah] and maftir, if one can stop there, they take out another, as Magen Avraham wrote, letter 16. And now I saw in Eshel Avraham, letter 16, he noticed this — see there. And see Levush Yoreh Deah 279; and here too the reason is since it is an enactment of the prophets.

And the rest of the matters will be explained below in Magen Avraham, letter 7, section 9; and here one need not elaborate further.

Another point I will speak: Eshel Avraham wrote here that the letter hei was found as a complete word doubled — they take out another, for all extra [letters] are considered as removed. And to me this requires study; for perhaps in such a case one may say: whatever is fit for soaking, like a letter stuck to a letter — so here; and even if one holds that extra is considered removed — in treifot they rule thus completely, unlike here — and this requires study.

The lay scribe said: All that I heard from my rabbis, and some of what was taught to me from Heaven, I wrote down — surely five Torah scrolls, long and wide as the sea; and, with God's help, the corruption of the times [has damaged them]. And every God-fearing man should be careful about this, especially scribes of STaM; go and see what Tzitz Eliezer wrote in siman 119: after he ruled, he feared perhaps he had not aimed correctly according to halakha, and he was great in his generation — and what will they answer for us today? Therefore let every man fear for his soul before ruling a halakhic matter, and the like.

mechaber.he: אפילו בכפרים שאין נמצא להם ס"ת כשר אין מברכין עליו:
mechaber.en: Even in villages that do not a valid Torah scroll, they should not recite the blessing upon [reading from] it.

baer_heitev.he: עליו. וקאי אסעיף ב' אם כתוב כל חומש לבדו:
baer_heitev.en: on him. And Kai B is written if it is written by each wall alone:

beur_hagra.he: ס"ג אפי' כו'. קאי אס"ב אחומשין בגלילה דלא כמרדכי שכתב בה"ק דכיון שאמרו מפני כבוד הציבור אם מחלו על כבודם ש"ד וכ"ש בכה"ג אבל בירושלמי דפ"ג דמגילה אמרו מגו דנפשיהון הוי עגומה אינון זבנין תורה אבל בב"י משמע דקאי אחומשין שלנו כמ"ש בשם תשובת הרשב"א ע"ש שכתב ובסוף התשובה כתב וז"ל כו' אבל בש"ע לא הזכיר חומשים שלנו וצריך לו' דקאי אס"ת עצמה שאין מברכין עליה וע' ס"ד בהג"ה ובשעת הדחק כו':
beur_hagra.en: SG Afi' 20. Kai SB Achumshin in Galila Dela as Mordechai who wrote in H. K. Dakhion who said because of public honor if they suffer for their honor 24 and 24 in 23 but in Yerushalmi DPG Damgila they said Mego Danefshihon hoi guma inon zavnin Torah but in the 2i the meaning of Dakai Ahomshin is our kamsh in the name of the answer to the scribe of the Rashba according to which he wrote and at the end of the answer And Zal 20, but in siman 20 he did not mention our Pentacles, and he needs the Dekai of the OT itself, which is not blessed, and the OT in the Haga and in the hour of distress, 20:

mechaber.en: If an error was found in a Torah scroll during the reading, they should take out another Torah scroll and begin [reading] from the place where the error was found, and complete the [number of] readers [i.e. aliyot] that are over [and above] those that were read [in the Torah] that had an error. And if the error was found in the middle reading, the reader should finish [that] reading in a valid Torah and blesses [the closing blessing] after it, and should not go back to bless [that's recited] before. {Rama: Gloss: If they already read 3 verses along with [the verse that is in error] and it's possible to stop [where the error was found], they stop there and bless [the closing blessing] afterwards, and [then] they conclude the remaining count [of aliyot] in the other Torah scroll that they take out (Mordekhai - chapter 2 in Tractate Megillah). This - that we take out another [sefer Torah] - is specifically when a complete error is found, but if was only because of missing or extra letters, we don't take out another [sefer Torah], since our Torah scrolls are not so precise so as to say that the other one would be more valid (Agur and Piskei Mahari"a - siman 80 and Ria"z). And Mahari"l ruled that another Torah scroll should not be brought, and Beit Yosef ruled that another Torah scroll must be brought (and therefore, we need the above compromise). In an extenuating circumstance, where the congregation has only the invalid Torah scroll, and there is no one there who is able to fix it, there are those who say that it should be read from it and the blessings should be recited (Kol Bo and Abudarham), and some invalidate [it] (Teshuvat HaRashb"a 487 and 405?, and Maimoni on chapter 10 of Laws of a Torah Scroll). And if one of the chumashim [books of the Torah] is complete, without errors, one may be lenient and read from that specific chumash, even though there are errors in the others (Ra"n)}

biur_halacha.en:
(1) If an error is found in a Torah scroll, etc. — see Mishna Berurah where we evaluated the three views: the view of Shulchan Aruch, which is the view of Mahari Bei Rav; the view of Mordechai; and Rama's ruling between them; see Magen Avraham who sides to rule like Bach who adopted Mordechai's view [for it appears to me the main law is that when they take out another Torah scroll he must bless on it, and when he finishes reading there there is concern of an unnecessary blessing, for perhaps the law is they fulfill reading even in an invalid Torah scroll, and therefore the first blessing was proper and now it is an unnecessary blessing when he blesses again on those same verses; but his view is also very difficult, for Mordechai himself holds for the law they fulfill in an invalid Torah scroll as is evident in his words — it is only because written matters may not be said orally, not because it is invalid, and therefore he permits finishing reading there; but we who are stringent not to read l'chatchila even where we have no valid Torah scroll, because most poskim hold they do not fulfill reading thereby — how can we permit l'chatchila to bless the final blessing, which for them is certainly a blessing in vain due to causing an unnecessary blessing afterward; I found this difficulty already raised by the gaon Maharaz Margaliot in his Pitchei Shearim]; behold the Gra's view in his commentary is also like Mordechai, that when he takes another Torah scroll he must bless on it; proof for this from that of chapter Ba Lo brought in Mordechai, and on this he wrote that on this proof there is no response; but on the main law of Mordechai who holds he finishes reading in the invalid book and blesses afterward — he certainly does not hold like him, for he holds the main law is like the poskim that they do not fulfill reading even b'dieved in an invalid Torah scroll and must return to the head in a valid Torah scroll, and therefore when he blesses there there is no unnecessary blessing, for the first blessing he blessed earlier is as one who did not bless, as Raosh wrote in his teshuvah; and behold though in early generations the custom in several places was to return to the head, as Tashbetz wrote and as the Gra's view, nevertheless now per how Shulchan Aruch books spread, it appears from later authorities that in all places the custom spread as Mahari Bei Rav taught, not to return to the head of the order, for b'dieved what they already read we rely on some lenient poskim; but if he is still in the middle of reading and an error is found, there are divided opinions and divided customs — some places spread custom only as Shulchan Aruch and Rama's ruling, as Shakh wrote Yoreh Deah siman 279; some places spread custom as Mordechai, as brought in Magen Avraham; and in truth where custom is established it is very hard to change custom, for each has whom to rely on, and we may read for them "and your people are all righteous," as Shaarei Ephraim wrote; but where no fixed custom is established, it appears from Magen Avraham one should conduct as Mordechai, and Chayei Adam and Darkhei Chochmah copied [Chayei Adam's words are very difficult, for he wrote in siman 133: if error found in Torah scroll later authorities ruled (see Magen Avraham siman 143 and Gra's commentary) where no fixed custom, if error in middle of reading even if not yet read three verses, read error orally and complete three times and bless at end, etc. see there — he copied all Magen Avraham's words; what he cited Gra's commentary implies therefore he adopted this view because Magen Avraham and Gra hold thus; in truth Gra does not hold thus to bless afterward, for it is blessing in vain per him; what he wrote that on Mordechai's proof there is no response is only that he must bless the first blessing when taking out Torah scroll, as I wrote above]; however many other later authorities all adopted for law as Shulchan Aruch ruled and Rama's ruling — Levush Yoreh Deah 279, Shakh there [Taz who holds main law like Shulchan Aruch], Avodat HaGershuni in name of several poskim, Nehar Shalom, R' Yehuda Ayash, Sefer Magen Giborim; therefore it is very correct to conduct l'chatchila per Shulchan Aruch and Rama where no fixed custom to the contrary; see Nehar Shalom who extended this; see Shaarei Ephraim who extended in Pitchei Shearim, and his view also not like Magen Avraham; he further wrote if they practiced that if a complete error is found in middle of reading not to read further and not to bless afterward in invalid scroll even if already read three times, but to roll this one without blessing afterward and take out another and bless blessing before it — they have what to rely on [and in truth this is view of most rishonim and Gra's view, except per them must return from head of order]; nevertheless it appears one need not begin from head of order, only begin from head of reading they read with this aliyah where error found; since otherwise he returns and blesses, good that he also read these verses in valid scroll with blessing, etc.; nevertheless not enough to re-read only those verses read in invalid, rather must add and read below them at least three verses — end of his words.

If an error is found. And Bach wrote, and these are his words: our custom according to Mordekhai — if he has not yet read three verses, he reads the error from memory until he reads three verses and stops there; and if it is less than three verses adjacent to the parasha, he completes the parasha; and so practiced the great ones of the world, the Ashkenazim before us. And Shulchan Aruch ruled this as a new ruling, and I did not know from where this ruling came — until here. And so too Maharal of Prague in Sefer Ner Yisrael daf 66: one word that has no meaning at all unless it is joined to another word is permitted to say from memory; and in truth the words of Shulchan Aruch have no basis except Mahari Bei Rav ruled thus, and as Rav Yaakov Bei Rav in Yoreh Deah siman 279 — the reason: since Rambam permits reading in an invalid Torah scroll, although we do not hold like him, nevertheless one may rely on him b'dieved that his reading is valid and he need not bless again. And his words require study, for even in a valid Torah scroll, if they take out another, one must bless — as is explicit in Yoma chapter 7, and so in siman 144, and so is implied by all the poskim (and see siman 215). If so, why does he not bless again? And Taz in Yoreh Deah strained to settle this — and therefore it appears to me that in a place where there is no custom, one should practice as Bach wrote, and in Massekhet Soferim chapter 11 halakhah 2 implies it is forbidden to read from memory; therefore they read in the invalid Torah scroll three verses and read the error from memory — siman 144. And in a place where there is a custom, it is difficult to change the custom; and in any case one should practice that if he began only the first word of the third verse, he should complete it and stop there, even if it is two verses adjacent to the parasha — he should read until the parasha, for it is better to push off this than to enter ourselves into doubt of a blessing mentioned explicitly in the Talmud, especially in a matter where Bach testified that the great ones practiced so. And in Levush on Laws of Torah Scroll, section 8, he wrote in the name of the Gaon Maharal of Prague that one should not take out another at all, as Beit Yosef wrote in Yoreh Deah siman 279 in the name of some poskim; therefore one may rely on them at least to complete the parasha with that in which the error was found. Rama wrote in Yoreh Deah siman 279, and these are his words: and there is no distinction in this between whether the error was found in the first Torah scroll or whether the error was found in the second that they read for the day's obligation for the maftir — until here. And his words are taken from what Beit Yosef wrote in siman 282 in the name of Rashbatz, and these are his words: a second Torah scroll in which an error was found — one must take out another Torah scroll, for the day's obligation is the maftir; and on every Shabbat, if a Torah scroll became invalid after they read seven — for example it was torn — it is possible, since the maftir reading is only on account of honor of the Torah, that therefore it suffices to read three verses in an invalid book without a blessing, so as not to burden the congregation; and one may question the matter — until here. And therefore Rama inferred and wrote in the second Torah scroll that they read for the day's obligation for the maftir, and he did not write generically "maftir" because it is doubtful to him; and if so it is clear one may rely on the great ones that I wrote above that one should not take out another; and not only that, but even if the error is found in the seventh [aliyah], he completes his reading in this Torah scroll and blesses after it, and he is the maftir — siman 282 s.k. 5, that we should not enter ourselves into dispute needlessly on account of an addition. And in this, siman 282, he inferred from the words of Rashbatz that if it occurred in the seventh after he read three verses, one should not take out another — because all his words are rejected, for it is clear one must read the entire order; for although there are places that practice to complete the order in another verse, nevertheless they read it on the coming Shabbat; if so, in any case they are obligated to read them; and so from what is written siman 137 s.k. 3, that even if he skipped one verse he returns — unlike the maftir, who reads only what they already read. And Taz in Yoreh Deah there wrote that if it is found in the seventh, he completes his reading and they take out another Torah scroll for the maftir at the time of saying Kaddish; and if the error is found in the maftir, he reads the error from memory — until here. And to my humble opinion, as I wrote: and it is clear he blesses after it; and see siman 215.

From the place where the error was found. Even if they did not know of the error until after they read three or four verses after the error — nevertheless they do not begin except from the place where they stopped, for b'dieved they fulfilled what they read in the invalid scroll.

And it is possible to stop — meaning that it is three verses before the parasha.

Missing and extra [letters]. Such as avotenu missing a vav, and the like; but an error where the reading of the word changed, such as kesev written as keves when it is known to be an error, even though it has one meaning — they take out another (Shlah). And in the responsum of R' Moshe of Lublin it is written: if it is written rachava instead of rachavo, it is considered a change of language, even though it is possible to read rachava with a kamatz like ohelah; nevertheless there too there is reason to discuss why it is written with a hei, as Rashi wrote there — unlike here — until here. And all this was unnecessary, for since it is a complete error they take out another; specifically for missing and extra letters we are not experts, as is stated in Kiddushin chapter 3; and if so, perhaps the other scroll is also not precise in missing and extra letters; but a complete error is clearly pasul, as stated above. Tzitz Eliezer wrote: if he erred and wrote misgerosam instead of misgereshem, he need not take out another, since we find sometimes thus, as we find in Ruth; and if a letter stuck to a letter, one may rely on Rashba who validates it and need not take out another (Bach siman 32); however Rashba validated only when the letter was written correctly and stuck at the end, but when it stuck in the middle, such as artzecha where the hei stuck in the middle — all the more so if it stuck at its head — Mode holds it is pasul, as written in teshuva siman 291.

And in a pressing circumstance. R' Moshe of Lublin ruled: if an error is found in a Torah scroll and there is no other, one completes the seven readers in this scroll and does not add to them; and for Minhah one does not remove it, for it is not the day's obligation, but only on account of the inhabitants of Keren HaRez — until here siman 84. And it appears to me that even in a place where it is an obligation, one should not remove it l'chatchila unless one chumash is complete, as Rama wrote here.

Errors in others. And so too Chayei Adam in Gittin daf 59 — the reason one does not read from chumashim is on account of honor of the congregation; and here it is permitted, since all are together, but there is an error in one.

פסוקים [וכ"ש כשלא קראו עדיין ג' פסוקים] וגם אפי' גמר קריאתו לגמרי כל שלא בירך עדיין ברכה אחרונה אין לברך ברכה אחרונה על הפסולה דזה הוא לכתחלה אלא יוציאו אחרת ויקראו שם ג' פסוקים ויברך שם ברכה אחרונה לבד זהו שיטת מהר"י בי רב שהעתיקו המחבר בסעיף זה. ודעת המרדכי שאם כבר קראו ג' פסוקים ואפשר להפסיק שם שאינו ב' פסוקים סמוך לפרשה פוסקים שם ומברך ברכה אחרונה ומוציאין אחרת לעלות שמה יתר הקרואים ואם עדיין לא קרא ג"פ או שקרא ג"פ אלא שנשאר רק ב"פ סמוך לפרשה שאי אפשר להפסיק שם יקרא הטעות בע"פ ויגמור קריאתו בפסולה ויברך ברכה אחרונה ואח"כ יוציא אחרת [וכן אם הוא בר"ח וכיוצא שצריך להשלים הפרשה לחובת היום ואין להוסיף על הקרואים וא"כ כשהטעות בקריאת הרביעי א"א להפסיק שמה לברך ברכה אחרונה שא"כ יצטרך להוסיף על מנין הקרואים וכיון שא"א להפסיק שמה יגמור הקריאה בספר הפסול ויברך ברכה אחרונה] והרמ"א בהג"ה עשה כעין הכרעה ביניהם והוא דאם לא קרא עדיין רק שני פסוקים או אפילו קרא ג"פ אך שא"א להפסיק שם כגון שהוא ב"פ סמוך לפרשה וכיו"ב לא יברך ברכה אחרונה אלא יוציא אחרת ויגמור קריאתו שמה ויברך ברכה אחרונה וכדעת המחבר אבל אם כבר קרא ג"פ והוא במקום שאפשר להפסיק שם דעתו כהמרדכי דיברך ברכה אחרונה על הפסולה ואח"כ יוציא אחרת ועתה נבוא לבאר דברי השו"ע בפרט:
(יד) בשעת קריאה - פי' שלא קראו עדיין רק מקצת העולין דבנשלם סדר הפרשה ואח"כ נמצא הטעות אין מוציאין אחרת דבדיעבד סמכינן אפוסקים דמכשירין קריאה בס"ת פסולה. ומיירי המחבר דנמצא הטעות בין גברי לגברי ולכך כל האנשים שכבר קראו עולין למנין ז' ואף האחרון דהוי דיעבד גמור:
(טו) ממקום שנמצא הטעות - מיירי שבמקום שפסק העולה שם נמצא הטעות ולהכי כתב דמתחילין ממקום זה וה"ה אפילו לא נודע להם הטעות עד אחר שקראו אחר הטעות ג' או ד' פסוקים ג"כ אין מתחילין אלא ממקום שפסקו דבדיעבד עלתה להם מה שקראו בספר הפסול [מ"א]:
(טז) על אותם וכו' - היינו דגם אותם שקראו כבר מצטרפין למנין שבעה וה"ה בשני וחמישי למנין שלשה ומ"מ אם אפשר לקרות ז' קרואים ממקום שפסקו עד סוף הסדרא ודאי ראוי ונכון לעשות כן לכתחלה [אחרונים]:
(יז) באמצע קריאת וכו' - היינו אפילו כבר קראו כמה פסוקים כל שלא בירך עדיין ברכה אחרונה אינו יכול לפטור עצמו במה שכבר קרא בס"ת הפסולה דזה הוי כלכתחלה שהרי יכול לקרות ג"פ בספר כשר וע"כ גומר וכו':
(יח) גומר קריאתו - היינו שיקרא שם שלשה פסוקים:
(יט) ואינו חוזר לברך וכו' - דס"ל דברכה ראשונה שבירך העולה בתחלת קריאתו בספר הראשון עולה גם לזו דהא דעתו היה מתחלה על פרשה זו מה לי ס"ת זו או אחרת:
(כ) לפניה - וה"ה כשנמצא הטעות בין ברכה לקריאה גוללין ס"ת זו ומוציאין ס"ת אחרת לקרות בה והעולה שכבר בירך א"צ לברך שנית אם לא הפסיק בשיחה בינתים ובמקום שנהגו בזה שהעולה חוזר ומברך ג"כ אין למחות בם שיש להם על מה שיסמוכו:
(כא) ואם כבר וכו' - דעה זו חולקת על המחבר כמו שכתבנו לעיל בהקדמה והו"ל לכתוב בלשון וי"א אלא שכן דרכו בכמה מקומות:
(כב) ואפשר להפסיק - פי' שהוא ג' פסוקים סמוך לפרשה דאם היה רק ב"פ סמוך לפרשה א"כ א"א לו לפסוק שם יגמור קריאתו בספר הכשר עד הפרשה וכנ"ל:
(כג) ומברך אחריה - דס"ל דכיון שקראו ג"פ קודם שנודע הטעות יצא בזה ידי קריאה וממילא צריך לברך אחריה וא"צ שוב לגמור קריאתו בספר הכשר אבל בשנמצא הטעות אחר שקראו רק ב"פ דא"א לו לפסוק שם מודה להמחבר דגומר קריאתו בספר הכשר ומברך אחריה. ועיין בבה"ל שבררנו בשם כמה אחרונים דכן יש לנהוג למעשה כפסק השו"ע וכפי מה שהכריע הרמ"א אם לא במקום שיש מנהג קבוע בעיר כדעת המ"א שתפס בשיטת המרדכי שהבאתי בהקדמה אין להם לשנות מנהגם. נוהגין שלא להוציא ס"ת אחרת בשביל מפטיר דהיינו אם נמצא טעות אחר שכבר קראו כל הסדרא קודם שאמרו קדיש לא יוציא ס"ת אחרת בשביל המפטיר וסמכינן בדיעבד על אותו שקרא אחרון שעולה גם בשביל מפטיר (ולא יקרא עוד הפעם בתורה) כדקיי"ל בסימן רפ"ב מפטיר עולה למנין שבעה והקדיש יאמר לאחר ברכות ההפטרה האחרונות ואם לא נודע הטעות עד לאחר שאמרו קדיש יקרא למפטיר בס"ת זו ג"פ בלא ברכה ולא יאמר קדיש עוד הפעם לאחר ההפטרה. ואם נמצא הטעות באמצע קריאת השביעי דעת מ"א שגומר הקורא עד סוף הסדרא בס"ת זו ועולה לו קריאה זו גם בשביל המפטיר כדקיי"ל בסימן רפ"ב וכנ"ל ויברך לאחריה ואח"כ יפטיר בנביא ואח"כ יאמר קדיש והרבה אחרונים חולקין על זה וסוברין דאין חילוק בין טעות שנמצא בשביעי לטעות שנמצא בשאר הקרואים ולכן אם לא קרא עדיין ג"פ גומר קריאתו בספר הכשר ואם כבר קרא ג"פ בשביעי וה"ה באחרון פוסק ומברך ויקרא לאחר בס"ת כשר ממקום שפסק והלאה ומשמע ממגן גבורים דכן יש לנהוג אם לא במקום שנהגו בזה כהמ"א. ואם נמצא הטעות לאחר שקראו שבעה וכבר בירך באחרונה ועדיין לא קראו כל הסדרא לכו"ע צריך להוציא אחרת שהרי על כרחך צריכין להשלים כל הסדרא ויקראו בשניה בברכה ויכולין להוסיף כשאר שבתות. אם נמצא טעות בס"ת בשעת קריאת המפטיר בשבת יגמור קריאתו ולא יברך אחריה וכל זה לענין מפטיר של שבת אבל בהפטרת יו"ט או של ארבע פרשיות וכיוצא שקריאת המפטיר בספר השני הוא לחובת היום ונמצא בו טעות יש להוציא אחרת כמו אם היה טעות בקריאת סדרא של שבת:
(כד) ומשלימים המנין - וה"ה שיכול להוסיף שמה ועיין לעיל בסקט"ז:
(כה) טעות גמור - כגון שהיה חסר או יתר תיבה או אות אחת או שהיה קרי במקום כתיב או פתוחה במקום סתומה או להיפוך וכן אם כתב פתוחה או סתומה במקום שא"צ או שחיסרה בכל אלו צריך להוציא אחרת וה"ה אם נמצא שתי תיבות שלא הרחיק כראוי עד שתינוק דלא חכים ולא טיפש קורא כתיבה אחת או להיפוך שהרחיק באמצע התיבה עד שנראה לתינוק הנ"ל כשתי תיבות או כדרלעמר פדהצור אליצור עמינדב וכהנה שמקובל בידנו שתיבה אחת היא אם נמצא בשתי שיטות צריך להוציא אחרת. אותיות ותיבות שנמחקו קצת אם רישומן ניכר שתינוק דלא חכים ולא טיפש יכול לקרותן א"צ להוציא אחרת [ואפילו לכתחלה מותר] אבל אם הוסר הדיו השחור ונשאר מראה אדמדם הוי שינוי מראה ופסול כ"כ בדה"ח בשם א"ר ועיין במה שכתבנו לעיל בסימן ל"ב במ"ב סקכ"ח בשם החתם סופר ובפרט לענין להוציא אחרת בודאי אין להחמיר בזה. נקרעו התפירות שבין יריעה ליריעה אפילו נקרע הרוב ועדיין מחוברת בחמש או בשש תפירות של קיימא כשר אבל בפחות מזה יש להוציא אחרת (מיהו מה שנמצא נקרע בחומש אחד מן החומשים בס"ת זו אין לפסול שאר החומשים לקרות בהם כמו שיתבאר בסוף ההג"ה). אם בשעת הקריאה נמצא אות אחד דבוק לחבירו אם הדביקות הוא בכל אורך האות או שנשתנה צורת האות ע"י הדביקות או שטעה וכתב דל"ת במקום רי"ש או בי"ת במקום כ"ף בכל אלו דינם כטעות גמור שצריך להוציא אחרת ואפילו אם ע"י דבוק זה לא נתקלקל אות השורש רק אות השימוש כגון וי"ו או יו"ד המשמשת אם אין שם דבק באורך האות רק מעט ולא נשתנה צורת האותיות וניכרים היטב לכתחלה אין להוציא ס"ת זו לקרות בה כ"ז שלא גררו הדבק ואם לא נודע והוציאו ס"ת ונמצא בשעת קריאה אם הדביקות בסוף האות שאם יגררו הדבק לבד יהיה חוזר להכשרו אזי בחול שאפשר לגרר ונקל לעשותו אף בשעת קריאה יש לגרר ויקרא להלן ואם אין שם מי שיכול לגרר בקל ובלי הפסד וקלקול ויש טורח צבור לחזור אחר מי שיגרור במתון או אם אירע בשבת שא"א לגרור מותר לקרות בו כך ואם הדביקות הוא בתחלת כתיבת האות או באמצעה שממקום הדיבוק ולהלן נכתב בפסול יש להוציא אחרת אף דלא נשתנה צורת האות עי"ז ויש מקילין שא"צ להוציא אחרת אף באופן זה כיון שלא נשתנה צורת האות עי"ז (ואף דמ"מ צריך גרירה קי"ל כל הראוי לבילה אין בילה מעכבת בו ודינו כאלו כבר נגרר ואפילו בשבת שא"א לגרור מכח איסור שבת מ"מ כיון שאינו מחמת הספר אלא איסור שבת רביע עליה א"צ להוציא אחרת) ובשעת הדחק שאין שם אחרת וצריך שהות להביא ממקום אחר ס"ת כשרה יש לסמוך ע"ז לגמור הקריאה בס"ת זו. אם נטף שעוה על איזה אות עיין לעיל בסימן ל"ב בבה"ל מה שכתבתי בשם דה"ח ובסימן ש"מ במ"ב סק"י ועיין דעת שערי אפרים בזה בשער ה' אות ז'. ויש עוד הרבה אופנים שצריך להוציא ס"ת אחרת על ידם אך קצרה היריעה מהכילם ימצאם המעיין בפמ"ג ובספר שערי אפרים בשער ה' ו' ובדרך החיים אך נקוט האי כללא בידך כל מקום שהוזכר בהלכות ס"ת שהוא פסול ודאי יש להוציא אחרת ודבר שהוא מחלוקת הפוסקים יש להקל לענין קריאת התורה שלא להוציא אחרת (מאחר דיש קצת פוסקים המקילין לקרות בס"ת פסולה):
(כו) משום חסרות ויתרות וכו' - כגון ווי"ן או יודי"ן מלאים או חסרים שלא נשתנה בהם הענין והמבטא כגון במקום שהיה צריך לכתוב אבותינו מלא וי"ו ונמצא חסר או להיפוך וכן במקום שהיה צריך לכתוב מלא ביו"ד שימושית ונמצא חסר או להיפוך אבל טעות שנשתנה במבטא אף שלא נשתנה הענין כגון כבש שהיה כתוב במקום כשב או שלמה שמלה צריך להוציא אחרת וכן ה"ה אם כתב מגרשיהן במקום מגרשיהם דהא איכא שינוי לשון וכן אם כתב רחבה במקום רחבו צריך להוציא אחרת אע"ג דנוכל לקרות בחולם כמו אהלה וכן בפסוק והנה תומים בבטנה אם כתב תומים מלא באלף תאומים אע"ג שהענין אחד צריך להוציא אחרת שהרי נרגש במבטא וכן בתיבת ונחנו מה אם כתב ואנחנו מה וה"ה אם נשתנה הענין עי"ז אע"ג שלא נשתנה במבטא כגון בתיבת ונמצה דמו כתב ונמצא דמו או בתיבת מאן יבמי שהוא שרש מיאון כתב מאין ביו"ד וכן כל כיוצא בזה צריך להוציא אחרת ועיין בדה"ח ובשערי אפרים שהאריכו בפרטים אלו:
(כז) אין להוציא אחרת - וה"ה אותיות גדולות וקטנות שנמסרו במסורה או עייני"ן הפוכות או פאי"ן כפופות וכה"ג שנמסרו במסרה לא שינוי מקרי להוציא אחרת דלא עדיף מחסרות ויתרות הנ"ל. וכן אם נמצא חסר הנקודות שיש בס"ת לפעמים כמו איה שרה אשתך דוירא וכיוצא בו שראוי להיות שם נקודות ע"פ המסורה אם נחסרו הנקודות א"צ להוציא אחרת:
(כח) צריך לחלק כך - היינו דרך הכרעה דדעת האגור דאפילו בטעות גמור אין מוציאין דלא ירויח דגם ס"ת אחרת אפשר דפסול בחסרות ויתרות ודעת הב"י דאפילו בחסרות ויתרות מוציאין וע"כ הכריע הרמ"א לנפשיה זה החילוק להלכה:
(כט) ויש פוסלין - הוא כדעת המחבר לעיל בס"ג וכן סתמו האחרונים דלכתחלה לא יוציאו אפילו לחובת היום. אמנם אם התחילו לקרות ואח"כ נמצא בה טעות ואין שם ס"ת אחרת זולתה י"א דגומרין ז' קרואים ומברכין לפניה ולאחריה רק המפטיר יהיה השביעי והקדיש יאמרו אחר ההפטרה. והדגול מרבבה כתב דאין להרבות בברכות באופן זה וכן כתב בשערי אפרים שער ו' אות ס"א אלא ישלים עם העולה הזה שנמצא אצלו הטעות הפרשה שלו ולא יברך ברכה אחרונה רק יעמוד שם והש"ץ יקרא לעולים אחרים עד תשלום ז' עולים ולא יברכו כלל רק הש"ץ יקרא לכל אחד פרשה שלו עד גמר הסדרה וזה העולה שנמצא הטעות בקריאה שלו העומד שם לא יסיח דעתו ויקרא בלחש עמהם ובגמר הסדרה יברך הוא ברכה האחרונה והוא יאמר גם כן ההפטרה בנביא בברכותיה ויש מי שכתב שיאמר ההפטרה בלי ברכות עכ"ל (ועיין בפתחי שערים שכתב שגם הדגמ"ר מודה בכל זה ע"ש). ואם נמצא הטעות בשלישי או בשאר העולין אחר סיום קריאתן שבירכו ברכה אחרונה ואין שם ס"ת אחרת זולתה יקרא הקורא שאר הפרשיות עד גמר הסדרא בלא ברכה:
(ל) חומש אחד וכו' - היינו שכל הס"ת הוא בגליון אחד אלא שאין שלם בלי טעות אלא חומש אחד אבל אם אין שם כ"א חומש אחד לכו"ע אין קורין בו וכדלעיל בס"ב:
(לא) יש להקל - היינו אפילו לדעת היש פוסלין הנ"ל דאסרי אפילו בשעת הדחק כל זה הוא אם הפסול נמצא באותו חומש שרוצה לקרות בו אבל בחומשין השלמים אין להחמיר בשעת הדחק כיון שעכ"פ בחלק זה שהוא קורא בו הוא שלם ולא דמי לחומש אחד שפסול לכו"ע לקרות בו וכדלעיל בס"ב שאני התם שאינו כבוד לצבור לקרות בחומש אחד משא"כ הכא שיש כל החמשה חומשין ביחד:

(13) If an error is found, etc. — in order to understand the words of this seif, I will precede it with a short introduction. Behold, the view of most poskim is that a Torah scroll missing one word or one letter, or in which an error is found, is pasul to read from; and according to them, if an error is found in it, even after they already read seven readers, one must return to the beginning in a valid Torah scroll and bless upon it, for that first reading is as if it never existed. And the view of some poskim is that even if several verses are missing — and all the more when an error is found in it in general — although it is not called a Torah scroll for fulfilling in it the positive mitzvah of writing a Torah scroll, nevertheless it is permitted to read from it if one has no other. And behold, the author in seif 3 ruled plainly that l'chatchila one should not take out an invalid Torah scroll to bless upon it, even in a place where one has no other, after the majority of poskim hold it is forbidden. However, if the error was found after they already read the sedra, Mahari Bei Rav ruled that for b'dieved one relies on the view of some of the aforementioned poskim who validate reading in it, and their reading is valid, and they need not take out another Torah scroll; and the acharonim agreed with him in this. And the same is true if the error was found between one man and another, and they have not yet completed the seven readers: regarding what they already read, one relies on the view of those who are lenient that they fulfilled b'dieved; but to read further in it is forbidden, and they take out another and begin from the place where the reading stopped, and complete the readers with those first ones who read in the erroneous scroll — meaning that they too join the seven readers, since it is b'dieved, as stated [and the acharonim wrote that nevertheless, if possible, it is better that they read seven readers in the Torah scroll they took out]. And all this if he already recited the closing blessing on the invalid scroll. But if in the middle of his reading they found an error, even if they already read many verses [and all the more when they have not yet read three verses], and even if he finished his reading entirely — as long as he has not yet recited the closing blessing, one does not recite the closing blessing on the invalid scroll, for this is l'chatchila; rather they take out another and read there three verses, and bless the closing blessing there alone. This is the method of Mahari Bei Rav that the author brought in this seif. And the view of Mordekhai is that if they already read three verses and it is possible to stop there — not being two verses adjacent to the parasha — they stop there and bless the closing blessing, and take out another for the remaining readers to ascend from there. And if he has not yet read three verses, or he read three verses but only two verses remain adjacent to the parasha where it is impossible to stop — he reads the error from memory and completes his reading in the invalid scroll and blesses the closing blessing, and afterward takes out another [and likewise if it is Rosh Chodesh and the like, where they must complete the parasha for the day's obligation and cannot add readers — if so, when the error is in the fourth reading, it is impossible to stop there to bless the closing blessing, for then they would need to add to the count of readers; and since it is impossible to stop there, he completes the reading in the invalid book and blesses the closing blessing]. And Rama in the gloss made a compromise between them: if he has not yet read only two verses, or even if he read three verses but cannot stop there — such as when it is two verses adjacent to the parasha and the like — he does not bless the closing blessing, but takes out another and completes his reading there and blesses the closing blessing, as the author's view; but if he already read three verses and is in a place where it is possible to stop there, his view is like Mordekhai: he blesses the closing blessing on the invalid scroll, and afterward takes out another. And now we come to explain the words of Shulchan Aruch in detail.

(14) At the time of reading — meaning they have not yet read except some of those called up; and when the order of the parasha is finished and afterward the error is found, they do not take out another, for b'dieved we rely on the poskim who validate reading in an invalid Torah scroll. And the author speaks when the error was found between one man and another [aliyah]; and therefore all the men who already read are counted for the number of seven, and even the last one, which is complete b'dieved.

(15) From the place where the error was found — it speaks when at the place where the oleh stopped, there the error was found; and therefore he wrote that they begin from this place. And the same is true even if they did not know of the error until after they read three or four verses after the error — likewise they do not begin except from the place where they stopped, for b'dieved they fulfilled what they read in the invalid scroll [Magen Avraham].

(16) Over those, etc. — meaning that also those who already read join the count of seven; and the same on Monday and Thursday for the count of three. And nevertheless, if it is possible to read seven readers from the place where they stopped until the end of the sedra, it is certainly fitting and proper to do so l'chatchila [acharonim].

(17) In the middle of the reading, etc. — meaning even if they already read several verses, as long as he has not yet recited the closing blessing, he cannot exempt himself with what he already read in the invalid Torah scroll, for this is l'chatchila, since he can read three verses in a valid scroll; and therefore he finishes, etc.

(18) He finishes his reading — meaning that he reads there three verses.

(19) And he does not go back to bless, etc. — for he holds that the first blessing with which the oleh blessed at the beginning of his reading in the first scroll applies also to this one, for his intent was from the start on this parasha — what difference to me whether this Torah scroll or another.

(20) Before it — and the same when the error is found between the blessing and the reading: they roll up this Torah scroll and take out another to read in it; and the oleh who already blessed need not bless again unless he interrupted with speech in the meantime. And in a place where they practiced that the oleh also goes back and blesses, one should not protest them, for they have what to rely on.

(21) And if they already, etc. — this opinion disputes the author, as we wrote above in the introduction; and it should have been written in the language of "some say," except that such is his way in many places.

(22) And it is possible to stop — meaning that it is three verses adjacent to the parasha; for if it were only two verses adjacent to the parasha, he cannot stop there — he completes his reading in the valid scroll until the parasha, as stated above.

(23) And he blesses after it — for he holds that since they read three verses before the error became known, he fulfilled his reading by this; and therefore he must bless after it, and he need not again finish his reading in the valid scroll. But when the error was found after they read only two verses, where he cannot stop there, he agrees with the author that he finishes his reading in the valid scroll and blesses after it. And see Biur Halacha, where we clarified in the name of several acharonim that one should practice thus per the ruling of Shulchan Aruch and as Rama decided — unless in a place where there is a fixed custom in the city, per Magen Avraham who adopted the method of Mordekhai that I brought in the introduction; they should not change their custom. The practice is not to take out another Torah scroll on account of the maftir — meaning, if an error is found after they already read the entire sedra before they said Kaddish, they do not take out another Torah scroll on account of the maftir; and b'dieved we rely on the one who read last, who also ascends for maftir (and he does not read again in the Torah), as is decided in siman 282 that the maftir counts for the number seven; and Kaddish is said after the closing blessings of the haftara. And if the error was not known until after they said Kaddish, the maftir reads in this scroll again without a blessing, and they do not say Kaddish again after the haftara. And if the error is found in the middle of the reading of the seventh [aliyah], Magen Avraham's view is that the reader completes until the end of the sedra in this scroll, and this reading counts for him also for maftir, as is decided in siman 282 and as above; and he blesses after it, and afterward he reads the haftara from the Prophets, and afterward he says Kaddish. And many acharonim dispute this and hold there is no distinction between an error found in the seventh and an error found in the other readers; and therefore, if he has not yet read three verses, he finishes his reading in the valid scroll; and if he already read three verses in the seventh — and the same in the last [aliyah] — he stops and blesses, and reads afterward in a valid Torah scroll from where he stopped onward. And it is implied from Magen Gibborim that one should practice thus, unless in a place where they practiced as Magen Avraham. And if the error is found after they read seven and he already blessed at the last [aliyah], but they have not yet read the entire sedra — per all opinions they must take out another, for perforce they must complete the entire sedra; and they read in the second with a blessing, and they may add [aliyot] as on other Shabbatot. If an error is found in a Torah scroll at the time of the maftir's reading on Shabbat, he completes his reading and does not bless after it; and all this is regarding the Shabbat maftir. But in the haftara of Yom Tov or of the four parshiyot and the like, where the maftir's reading in the second scroll is the day's obligation — if an error is found in it, one takes out another, as if there were an error in reading the Shabbat sedra.

(24) And they complete the count — and the same, that one may add from there; and see above s.k. 16.

(25) A complete error — such as a word or letter was missing or extra, or it was read as kri instead of ketiv, or open instead of closed or the reverse; and likewise if he wrote open or closed where it was not needed, or it was missing — in all these one must take out another. And the same if two words were not spaced properly until a child who is neither wise nor foolish reads them as one writing, or the reverse — that he spaced in the middle of the word until it appears to such a child as two words; or as in "pedah-tzur eli-tzur ammi-ndav," and the like, which is accepted among us as one word — if it is found in two lines, one must take out another. Letters and words that were erased somewhat — if their outline is visible so that a child who is neither wise nor foolish can read them, one need not take out another [and even l'chatchila it is permitted]. But if the black ink was removed and a reddish appearance remains, this is a change of appearance and it is pasul — so in Darkei Chayim in the name of Acharonim; and see what we wrote above in siman 32, Mishna Berurah s.k. 288, in the name of Chatam Sofer; and especially regarding taking out another, certainly one should not be stringent about this. If the stitches between one sheet and another were torn — even if most was torn but it is still connected by five or six enduring stitches, it is kosher; but with less than that, one should take out another (however, what was found torn in one chumash of the chumashim in this Torah scroll does not invalidate the other chumashim to read from them, as will be explained at the end of the gloss). If at the time of reading one letter was found stuck to its fellow — if the adhesion is along the entire length of the letter, or the form of the letter was changed by the adhesion, or he erred and wrote a dalet instead of a reish, or a bet instead of a kaf — in all these their law is like a complete error that requires taking out another; and even if through this adhesion the root letter was not corrupted but only a servile letter, such as vav or yud used as a vowel — if there is no adhesion along the length of the letter, only a little, and the form of the letters was not changed and they are well recognizable — l'chatchila one should not take out this Torah scroll to read from it as long as they have not scraped off the glue. And if it was not known and they took out the scroll and the error is found at the time of reading — if the adhesion is at the end of the letter, so that if they scrape off the glue alone it will return to its validity, then on a weekday when it is possible to scrape and it is easy to do, even at the time of reading one may scrape and read onward. And if there is no one who can scrape easily without loss and damage, and there is burdening of the congregation to wait for one who will scrape slowly, or if it occurred on Shabbat when scraping is impossible — it is permitted to read in it thus. And if the adhesion is at the beginning of writing the letter or in its middle, so that from the place of adhesion onward it was written invalid — one should take out another, even though the form of the letter was not changed thereby; and some are lenient that one need not take out another even in this manner, since the form of the letter was not changed thereby (and even though scraping is required — we hold that whatever is fit for soaking is not impeded by lack of soaking, and its law is as if it were already scraped; and even on Shabbat when scraping is impossible on account of Shabbat prohibition — nevertheless, since it is not on account of the scroll but a Shabbat prohibition, one need not take out another). And in a pressing circumstance, where there is no other scroll and time is needed to bring a valid Torah scroll from elsewhere, one may rely on this to complete the reading in this scroll. If wax dripped on some letter, see above siman 32 in Biur Halacha what I wrote in the name of Darkei Chayim, and siman 340, Mishna Berurah s.k. 10; and see the view of Shaarei Ephraim on this in section 5, letter 7. And there are many more cases where one must take out another Torah scroll on their account; but the scroll is too short to contain them — the investigator will find them in Peri Megadim and in Sefer Shaarei Ephraim sections 5 and 6, and in Derekh HaChayim. But take this rule in your hand: wherever it is mentioned in the laws of a Torah scroll that it is certainly pasul, one must take out another; and a matter that is disputed among the poskim, one may be lenient regarding Torah reading not to take out another (since there are some poskim who are lenient to read in an invalid Torah scroll).

(26) On account of missing and extra [letters], etc. — such as vavs or yuds that are full or missing, where the meaning was not changed and the pronunciation — such as where it should have been written avotenu full with a vav and it was found missing, or the reverse; and likewise where it should have been written full with a servile yud and it was found missing, or the reverse. But an error where the pronunciation changed, even though the meaning did not change — such as keves that was written instead of kesev, or Shlomo that is a complete word — one must take out another. And the same if he wrote misgereshem instead of misgerosam, for there is a change of language; and if he wrote rachava instead of rachavo, one must take out another, even though we can read it with a kamatz like ohelah; and likewise in the verse "ve-hineh tomim be-vitnah," if he wrote tomim full with an aleph as te'omim, even though the meaning is one — one must take out another, for the pronunciation is stirred; and likewise in the word venachnu mah, if he wrote ve-anachnu mah; and the same if the meaning changed thereby even though the pronunciation did not change — such as in the word venimtza damo, if he wrote venimtze damo; or in the word ma'an yevami, which is the root of refusal, if he wrote me'ayin with a yud; and all similar cases require taking out another. And see Darkei Chayim and Shaarei Ephraim, who elaborated on these details.

(27) One does not take out another — and the same for large and small letters transmitted in the mesorah, or inverted ayin, or bent pei, and the like transmitted in the mesorah — this is not a change of pronunciation to take out another, for they are no better than the aforementioned missing and extra letters. And likewise if the nekudot that are sometimes in a Torah scroll are missing — such as in "ei Sarah ishtekha" that should have nekudot per the mesorah — if the nekudot are missing, one need not take out another.

(28) One must compromise thus — meaning, this is the way of resolution: the view of Agur is that even in a complete error one does not take out another, for one does not gain, since the other Torah scroll too may be pasul through missing and extra letters; and the view of Beit Yosef is that even for missing and extra letters one takes out another; and therefore Rama personally decided this distinction as halakha.

(29) And some invalidate — this is like the author's view above in s.k. 3; and so the acharonim ruled plainly that l'chatchila they do not take out another, even for the day's obligation. However, if they began to read and afterward an error was found in it, and there is no other Torah scroll besides it — some say they complete seven readers and bless before and after it; only the maftir should be the seventh, and they say Kaddish after the haftara. And Dagul MeRevavah wrote that one should not multiply blessings in this manner; and so Shaarei Ephraim wrote, section 6, letter 61 — rather, he completes with this oleh in whose reading the error was found his parasha, and he does not bless the closing blessing; he only stands there, and the prayer leader calls the other olelim until seven olelim are completed, and they do not bless at all; only the prayer leader reads for each one his parasha until the sedra is finished. And this oleh in whose reading the error was found, standing there, does not distract his attention and reads in a whisper with them; and at the end of the sedra he blesses the closing blessing, and he also says the haftara from the Prophets with its blessings. And there is one who wrote that he says the haftara without blessings — until here (and see in Pitchei She'arim, who wrote that Dagul MeRevavah also agrees to all this — see there). And if the error is found in the third [aliyah] or in the rest of the olelim after they finished their reading and blessed the closing blessing, and there is no other Torah scroll besides it — the reader reads the rest of the parshiyot until the sedra is finished without a blessing.

(30) One chumash, etc. — meaning that the entire Torah scroll is in one scroll, but it is not complete without error except for one chumash; but if there is only one chumash there, per all opinions one does not read from it, as above in seif 2.

(31) One may be lenient — meaning, even per the view of "some invalidate" who forbid even in a pressing hour — all this is when the disqualification is in that chumash from which he wants to read; but in the complete chumashim one need not be stringent in a pressing hour, since in any case in this portion in which he reads it is complete; and it is not comparable to one chumash that is pasul per all opinions to read from it — and as above in seif 2, for there it is different, since it is not honor of the congregation to read from one chumash, unlike here where all five chumashim are together.

(32) To read — meaning, with a blessing; and see Biur Halacha.

ואם כבר קראו עמו ג' פסוקים. תמוהים דבריו דהרכיב תרי דיעות ביחד בתרתי. חדא דלדעת הש"ע אפי' תוך ג"פ ישלים בס"ת אחרת בלא ברכה שאחריה אלא ימתין בברכה עד שישלים בס"ת אחרת והיא דעת רבו של ב"י מהר"י בי רב ולדעת הגה זו שהיא מהמרדכי פ"ב דמגילה יאמר החסרון או הפסול בעל פה וישלים עד ג"פ ויברך אחריה ויוציא אחרת. שנית דלדעת מהר"י בי רב אפי' כבר קרא ג"פ לא יברך אחריה אלא יוציא ס"ת אחרת וגומר ולדעת המרדכי צריך לברך אחריה בס"ת הפסולה ואח"כ יוציא אחר' וא"כ היה לו לכתוב וי"א דאם כבר קראו ג"פ ובלבוש כתוב כאן וי"א ובי"ד סימן רע"ט העלתי בס"ד לנהוג דאם נמצא הטעות תוך ג"פ לא יברך אחריה אלא יוציא אחרת וישלים ואח"כ יברך אחריה וא"צ ברכה ראשונה שנית על האחרת אלא סומך על מה שבירך בפסולה ואם לאחר ג"פ יברך אחריה ויוציא אחרת ואם נמצא הטעות במקום שא"א להפסיק כגון שלא ישתיירו ג"פ אח"ז או שהיא בקריאת האחרון שאין קור' אחריו אז ינהוג כהמרדכי ויאמר הטעות בע"פ וישלים בפסול' ואח"כ יברך אחרי' עיין בי"ד מ"ש ההוכחה ע"ז מצד דין התלמוד:
חסירות ויתרות. כגון ווי"ן או יודי"ן מלאים או חסרים וכ"כ בלבוש אבל לא תליא מילתא אם יש להם פי' א' כגון כבש וכשב בזה צריך להוציא אחרת דמ"מ תיבה אחרת היא ולא כפי מ"ש קצת בעלי בתים דבפי' המלה תליא מלתא וזה אינו. ופעם א' הייתי בדרך בק"ק סקאל בשבת שנמצא סדק באות א' באופן שהיא פסולה ולא היה שם ס"ת אחרת הוריתי לגמור מנין הקרואים באותו הס"ת שזה הסדק אינו נראה לעין בפירוש והוא שעת הדחק נראה דאף היש מחמירין שמבי' רמ"א מודים וכן ראיתי בתשובת ר"מ מלובלין שפסק בנחסר תיבה שלימה ולא הי' ס"ת אחרת שיגמור הקריאה באותו ס"ת כל זמן שלא קראו ז' גברי אבל אם נמצא כן אחר שקראו ז' יגמור אותו הקורא כל הסדרה:

And if they already read three verses along with it. His words are wondrous, for he combined two views together, one opposite the other. One: per Shulchan Aruch, even within three verses he completes in another Torah scroll without the blessing after it, but he waits with the blessing until he finishes in another Torah scroll — and this is the view of Mahari Bei Rav, the teacher of Beit Yosef. And per this gloss, which is from Mordekhai chapter 2 of Megillah, he says the missing or invalid portion from memory and completes until three verses and blesses after it, and takes out another. Second: per Mahari Bei Rav, even if he already read three verses he does not bless after it, but takes out another Torah scroll and completes; and per Mordekhai he must bless after it on the invalid Torah scroll, and afterward takes out another. If so, he should have written "some say": if they already read three verses. And in Levush he wrote here "some say"; and in Yoreh Deah siman 279 I raised in Saad to practice: if the error is found within three verses, he does not bless after it, but takes out another and completes, and afterward blesses after it; and he need not recite the opening blessing again on the other, but relies on what he blessed on the invalid one. And if after three verses — he blesses after it and takes out another. And if the error is found in a place where it is impossible to stop — such as three verses will not remain afterward, or it is in the reading of the last [aliyah], after whom there is no reading — then he should practice like Mordekhai: he says the error from memory and completes in the invalid scroll, and afterward blesses after it. See Yoreh Deah what proof he brought for this from the law of the Talmud.

Missing and extra [letters]. Such as vavs or yuds that are full or missing; and so in Levush. But the matter does not depend on whether they have one meaning, such as keves and kesev — in this one must take out another, for it is nevertheless a different word; and not as some householders said, that the matter depends on the meaning of the word — this is not so. And once I was traveling in the community of Skal on Shabbat, when a crack was found in one letter in a manner that it was pasul, and there was no other Torah scroll there — I ruled to complete the count of readers in that Torah scroll, for this crack was not visible to the eye explicitly; and it was a pressing hour — it appears that even those who are stringent, whom Rama brought, admit. And so I saw in the responsum of R' Moshe of Lublin, who ruled regarding a missing complete word, when there was no other Torah scroll, that he should complete the reading in that scroll as long as they had not read seven men; but if it is found thus after they read seven, that reader completes the entire sedra.

mishnah_berurah.he: (לג) שאין בהם וכו' - ר"ל שאינם יודעים לקרות אחרי הש"ץ מלה במלה מתוך הכתב והמחבר אזיל לטעמיה בסימן קל"ט ס"ב דכתב שם דבאופן זה לא יעלה אכן לפי מה שכתב הרמ"א שם (בסעיף ה')[בס"ג בהג"ה] דאנו קוראים אפילו לע"ה ואפילו אינו יכול לקרות אחרי המקרא וכמו שכתבנו שם במ"ב וא"כ ישתנה האי דינא דלדידן לעולם צריך לקרות שבעה קרואים ויברכו והש"ץ יוציאם בקריאתו וכן משמע בביאור הגר"א שם בס"ד ד"ה ומהרי"ל כדברינו:
mishnah_berurah.en: (33) That there are not, etc. — meaning that they do not know how to read after the prayer leader word by word from the writing; and the author follows his reasoning in siman 139, s.k. 2, where he wrote that in this manner it does not count. However, per what Rama wrote there (in seif 5) [in seif 2 in the gloss] that we read even for a gentile, and even if he cannot read after the prompting — as we wrote there in Mishna Berurah — if so, this law changes: for us, always seven readers must read and bless, and the prayer leader takes them out in his reading; and so is implied in the explanation of the Gra there in this seif, in the matter of "and Maharil," as we said.
